title: Aphelion launch and publishing workflow checkpoint
content:
Aphelion is now standing in the JeffersonWM network as a real split-deployment site instead of a loose imported experiment. Today's pass focused on turning it into a repeatable app surface with a clear division between ASO frontend hosting, home-server backend runtime, shared image-library access, and coordinated service startup.

The publishing and runtime side was the most important new infrastructure step. Aphelion now has a dedicated publish helper from the JeffersonWM monorepo, a live backend folder on the server share, task and launcher entries for both server and tunnel, a status-page presence, and a health endpoint that matches the rest of the network. We also cleaned up the Vite env handling so NODE_ENV stays in launch commands instead of the frontend env files, which removes the misleading build warning and keeps the server/frontend responsibilities cleaner.

The image-runtime side was brought into shape too. After confirming that the public site was falling back to placeholders whenever the live API could not read the Keep library, Aphelion's backend was updated to try multiple configured image roots in order, preferring the fast local server path and then falling back to the shared UNC path. Once the live API came up cleanly, the site began reading the real Keep catalog and displaying the shared image set instead of generated placeholders.

The UI pass then moved from infrastructure into browsing quality. The hover preview was enlarged into a fixed 768 by 768 square and switched to a browser-generated thumbnail cache so repeated hovers feel lighter without needing a second manually maintained thumbnail library. This keeps the user-facing behavior simple while avoiding a naive "load ten thousand full images at once" approach.

What changed in this checkpoint:

  • Added Aphelion to the JeffersonWM monorepo publish workflow with frontend upload plus backend sync to the server share.
  • Added Aphelion server and tunnel entries to the shared service launcher and the grouped VS Code task flows so it starts and restarts alongside the rest of the platform.
  • Added consistent /health and /api/health routes and linked Aphelion into the JeffersonWM status page.
  • Removed NODE_ENV from Aphelion env files and documented the cleaner launch pattern.
  • Updated Aphelion image-root handling so the backend can try a local server image path first and fall back to the shared Keep path.
  • Brought the live site onto the real Keep image library and replaced the placeholder fallback with actual catalog-backed browsing.
  • Resized the hover preview to a fixed square and added browser-side thumbnail caching for faster repeated preview use.

This is a strong first live checkpoint for Aphelion: the app now fits the JeffersonWM deployment model, reads the shared library, participates in the status/runtime system, and has a clearer path for future image-browser refinement.
